## Question 1: For the relation represented by all of the columns in the CSV file and the table in the SQLite database, define all functional dependencies and list them.

### Restaurants
$$
\begin{aligned}
\texttt{RestaurantID} &\to \texttt{RestaurantName},\ \texttt{City},\ \texttt{State},\ \texttt{hasTableService}
\end{aligned}
$$

### Servers
$$
\begin{aligned}
\texttt{ServerEmpID} &\to \texttt{ServerName},\ \texttt{StartDateHired},\ \texttt{EndDateHired},\ \texttt{HourlyRate}\\
\texttt{ServerEmpID} &\to \texttt{BirthDate},\ \texttt{SSN},\ \texttt{rID}\\
\texttt{SSN} &\to \texttt{ServerEmpID}
\end{aligned}
$$

### Customers
$$
\begin{aligned}
\texttt{CustomerEmail} &\to \texttt{CustomerName},\ \texttt{CustomerPhone},\ \texttt{LoyaltyMember}
\end{aligned}
$$

### Visits
Each row of the CSV is one visit, which determines the rest of the row.
$$
\begin{aligned}
\texttt{Visit} &\to \texttt{RestaurantID},\ \texttt{ServerEmpID},\ \texttt{CustomerEmail},\ \texttt{VisitDate},\ \texttt{VisitTime}\\
\texttt{Visit} &\to \texttt{MealType},\ \texttt{PartySize},\ \texttt{WaitTime}\\
\texttt{Visit} &\to \texttt{FoodBill},\ \texttt{TipAmount},\ \texttt{FoodDiscountPercentage},\ \texttt{PaymentMethod},\ \texttt{orderedAlcohol},\ \texttt{AlcoholBill}
\end{aligned}
$$

## Question 2: Using the functional dependencies and the rules of normalization, decompose the relational from the CSV and the SQLite database into several relations that all satisfy 3NF; give the relations reasonable names.

Original relational form:

- RestaurantVisits(RestaurantID, RestaurantName, City, State, hasTableService, ServerEmpID, ServerName, StartDateHired, EndDateHired, HourlyRate, BirthDate, SSN, CustomerName, CustomerPhone, CustomerEmail, LoyaltyMember, VisitDate, VisitTime, MealType, PartySize, WaitTime, FoodBill, TipAmount, FoodDiscountPercentage, PaymentMethod, orderedAlcohol, AlcoholBill)

Relations in 3NF:

- restaurants(rid, restaurantname, city, state, hastableservice)
- servers(empid, servername, startdatehired, enddatehired, hourlyrate, birthdate, ssn, rid)
- customers(cid, customername, customerphone, customeremail, loyaltymember)
- bill(billid, foodbill, tipamount, fooddiscountpercentage, pmid, orderedalcohol, alcoholbill)
- paymentmethods(pmid, paymentmethod)
- mealtypes(mtid, mealtype)
- visits(visitid, customerid, restaurantid, serverempid, billid, mtid, visitdate, visittime, partysize, waittime)

### Definitions
**1NF:**

1. All attributes must contain atomic (indivisible) values. This means that each attribute in the table can only hold a single value.
2. The relation must have no repeating groups of attributes or tuples. Each row must represent a single, distinct entity or concept.

**2NF:**

1. It is in 1NF.
2. All non-prime attributes (attributes that are not part of the primary key or any candidate key) are fully functionally dependent on the entire primary key, meaning there are no partial dependencies.

**3NF:**

1. It is in 2NF.
2. No transitive dependencies exist. A transitive dependency occurs when a non-prime attribute is functionally dependent on another non-prime attribute. A non-prime attribute is an attribute that is not part of any candidate key of a relation.

The original relation is in 1NF and 2NF because it has no repeating groups and the non-prime attributes depend on the entire primary key. However, values like RestaurantID repeat across many rows with their details, since non-prime attributes depend on other non-prime attributes ( RestaurantID -> RestaurantName). By breaking it down into multiple tables, including lookup tables, no transitive dependencies exist, allowing for 3NF.
